title: From quotes to a directed graph
summary: Turn bid and ask observations into reciprocal directed conversions and compare the two oriented loops.
transcript: A market triangle has three currency vertices.
Each quoted pair supplies a bid edge and a reciprocal-ask edge in the opposite direction.
A directed three-edge circuit adds log conversion rates. The score depends on the orientation and the per-leg cost.

title: Executions, books, and visible depth
summary: Compare a reported execution with a bid and ask ladder, then see which information depth makes possible.
transcript: An execution is a reported trade with a time, price, and quantity.
A book records visible quantities at bid and ask price levels. Its state changes with ordered updates.
The reconstructed book supports depth-aware replay. An archived book shows visible liquidity, and subscriber receipt timing remains unobserved.

title: The forecast data clock
summary: Put quote events, release availability, and the future target on a timeline.
transcript: Find the last eligible observation at the forecast anchor.
Different sources use different clocks. A report must be released before it can enter the input.
The later one-second observation is the target. Training, validation, stress, and test folds keep their chronological boundaries.

title: How a graph cellulates the torus
summary: Follow two marked loops on a rotating torus, then count faces, edges, and vertices.
transcript: Two generator loops mark the torus. They share a vertex and cut out a single disk.
Darts and a rotation system specify how edges meet and boundaries close.
The Euler characteristic counts vertices minus edges plus faces. A connected closed orientable surface with Euler characteristic zero has genus one.

title: Gauge changes and loop holonomy
summary: Watch local link coordinates change as their loop product stays fixed.
transcript: A local gauge change alters the phases on individual directed links.
Matching vertex factors cancel in the product around a closed loop.
On a torus, face loops and the two independent handle cycles carry distinct information.

title: The cyclic qudit clock and shift
link_label: Open the network and research tools
summary: Track basis states and phase as a clock and shift are applied in different orders.
transcript: A cyclic qudit has q basis states.
The clock multiplies a basis state by a phase. The shift moves it around a cycle.
With the displayed convention the two orders differ by a root-of-unity phase. An interference measurement can reveal relative phase.

title: Gauge transport and density
summary: Follow unitary transport and see why density can survive a basis change.
transcript: A node carries a vector with color components. Link maps transport these amplitudes.
Changing an internal color basis changes individual components.
Summing squared component magnitudes gives a local density unchanged by a unitary basis transformation.

title: A conserved density in motion
summary: Watch a three-dimensional density packet move along a plane while its integral stays fixed.
transcript: The height of the surface is an idealized positive density on a plane.
The packet moves at fixed velocity. Its value at position x and time t equals the initial density at x minus velocity times t.
The integral over the whole plane stays one. PhaseWeave’s unitary graph transport uses a related conservation principle with node and edge states.

title: Forest of Thought in a continuous space
link_label: Try the Forest of Thought controls
summary: Six continuous paths branch after shared updates and compete in the same density landscape.
transcript: Embed the observed graph into a real-valued state.
Three candidate contexts guide continuous updates. Each candidate splits after the shared initial updates.
Score all six endpoints under the same reward field. The highlighted path is the highest-scoring candidate under the displayed rule.

title: Analogical transport
summary: Move a reference displacement to a new query and vary the strength of the transfer.
transcript: A past example moves from an earlier embedding to a later embedding.
Take its displacement and attach the same vector to the query point.
A real-valued coefficient scales the transfer. Choosing an earlier source preserves the demonstration’s time boundary.

title: Steering a frozen graph encoder
summary: Change a real latent coefficient and see the measured shift in two October route forecasts.
transcript: Fit concept directions using frozen graph activations from the training cut.
Add a controlled displacement before the unchanged forecast readout.
The two margin outputs shift by different amounts. The measured response is a property of this model and this intervention.

title: Continuous GFlowNet trajectories
summary: Follow continuous Gaussian transitions and compare two trained seeds with an unconditional reference.
transcript: A positive reward gives the desired terminal density over real-valued states.
Draw an intermediate embedding and a terminal embedding from forward kernels. Backward densities enter the trajectory balance check.
Measured October terminal KL compares the learned conditional sampler with an unconditional Gaussian. The target density also admits direct Gaussian sampling.

title: How the graph network reads a market
summary: Trace a market graph through typed local messages, attention, a phase patch, and the two-margin readout.
transcript: Each directed edge carries its endpoints, log quote, age and availability.
Local graph layers pass real vectors along the permitted edges.
Token attention can join global graph context. A cyclic-qutrit patch adds phase features, and temporal layers pool the observed frames for the output.

title: Softmax and max-plus attention
summary: Work through an attention example with a weighted average and a componentwise maximum.
transcript: The schematic compares the same three example neighbor scores and values.
Softmax normalizes weights and averages all values.
Max-plus adds each score to its value and selects the componentwise maximum. The controlled benchmark compares the two rules on real forecasting windows.

title: What changed at larger model widths
summary: Watch the recorded validation measurements build and find the selected epoch for each of the three widths.
transcript: A proxy sweep fixes the shared recipe before transferring it to larger widths.
Points show actual validation errors across all full-pass convergence epochs.
The lowest validation MAE selects each width’s checkpoint. The October and CHF holdouts have separate results.

title: Run a forecast on observed evidence
summary: Inspect a recorded quote window, verify its availability, and compare the forecast with persistence and its recorded outcome.
transcript: Select an observed market window such as the October London session.
Check available edges, quote age, and cost assumptions.
Run a frozen checkpoint for next-second margins, then compare the prediction, persisted anchor margin, and later recorded margin.
